items.claim: `lfoValue(shape, timeMs, rate)` (engine/modulation.ts:8-21) and `continuousWave(waveform, p)` (voice/lfo.ts:72-84) independently implement the same four shapes with the same formulas — sine `0.5 + 0.5*sin(2πp)`, triangle `p<0.5 ? 2p : 2(1-p)`, saw `p`, square `p<0.5 ? 1 : 0`. They already disagree in scope: voice/lfo.ts adds a fifth waveform (`sample-hold`), bpm-synced rate via `computeDelayMs`, and a phase offset, none of which exist on the legacy side. A change to the shape vocabulary or to any waveform's curve is therefore a two-site edit with no compiler link between them.

evidence.detail: engine/modulation.ts:9-21 — `const phase = wrap(timeMs*0.001*rate,1)` then a switch over 'saw'|'square'|'triangle'|'sine' returning exactly the formulas listed above.

voice/lfo.ts:73-84 — `continuousWave` switch over 'sine'|'triangle'|'saw'|'square' with byte-equivalent expressions; LFO_WAVEFORMS (line 22) adds 'sample-hold', and lfoPeriodMs (line 57) adds beats-synced rate that the legacy copy has no notion of.

`grep -rn 'lfoValue|sourceValue|applyCurve' apps packages | grep -v src/engine/` returns nothing — the legacy modulation module has zero consumers outside packages/core/src/engine and its own test, confirming the two copies never meet.
evidence.command: grep -rn "resolveParams|sourceValue|lfoValue|applyCurve" apps packages | grep -v "src/engine/"

items.proposed_fix: Make voice/lfo.ts the single owner of waveform math and have engine/modulation.ts's `lfoValue` delegate: `lfoValue(shape, t, rate) => sampleLfo({ waveform: shape as LfoWaveform, rateMode: 'hz', rateHz: rate, division: '1/4', phase: 0 }, t, 0)`. If the legacy stack is deleted per the dual-stack finding, this duplication disappears with it — so sequence this after that decision.

removes_failure_path.justification: Delegating one pure math function to another pure math function removes no guard, validation, retry or fallback; the default-case behaviour of the legacy switch (unknown shape → sine) must be preserved explicitly in the delegation.

steps: Property-check equivalence before deleting: for shape in {sine,triangle,saw,square} and 1000 (t, rate) samples, assert `lfoValue(shape,t,rate) === sampleLfo({waveform:shape,rateMode:'hz',rateHz:rate,division:'1/4',phase:0}, t, 0)`.
Apply the delegation and run `pnpm --filter @ledrums/core run test` — engine/modulation.test.ts pins the legacy behaviour and must pass unchanged.
Confirm the unknown-shape default (legacy falls through to sine) still holds — sampleLfo has no default arm, so this needs an explicit guard in the delegation.

items.claim: Adding or changing one field on any wire payload requires three coordinated edits inside a single package: the hand-written `interface` in index.ts (21 exported interfaces/types between lines 45 and 300), the corresponding zod schema in schemas.ts, and — for any newly added payload — a `_Lock<Name> = Assert<Equals<z.infer<typeof …Schema>, …>>` line in schemas.ts:453-472. The lock assertions exist precisely because the two declarations can drift; they are a compile-time patch over a structural duplication that `z.infer` would eliminate outright.

evidence.detail: packages/protocol/src/index.ts:14-15 states outright: "The payload interfaces below (SerializedModel, EffectSpec, OutputStatus, …) are locked to their schemas by a type-level assertion in ./schemas" — the duplication is acknowledged in the source.

grep on index.ts finds 21 exported interfaces/types (ShowLibraryBlob:45, SongLibraryBlob:54, BackupSnapshotMeta:66, SerializedDrum:74, SerializedModel:82, EffectSpec:96, OutputStatus:105, VoiceStat:120, VoiceStats:137, ControllerUniverseRx:155, DiscoveredController:176, NetworkAdapter:195, ControllerTestPattern:216, ControllerStatus:232, MonitorEvent:258, TunnelInfo:278, OscListenInfo:293, …); schemas.ts:453-472 holds 15 matching `_Lock*` Assert lines.
evidence.command: grep -n "interface |^export type |z.infer" packages/protocol/src/index.ts; grep -n "_Lock" packages/protocol/src/schemas.ts

evidence.detail: Confirmed as a live scatter: fbd63a2 ('wire SnapshotStore') edits both packages/protocol/src/index.ts and packages/protocol/src/schemas.ts plus schemas.test.ts in one commit, alongside 5 server files.
evidence.command: for c in $(git log --format='%h' -200 -- packages/protocol/src/schemas.ts); do git show --name-only --format='' $c; done

items.proposed_fix: Invert the direction: keep the zod schemas as the sole declaration and replace each hand-written interface with `export type SerializedModel = z.infer<typeof serializedModelSchema>;` (doc comments move onto the type alias / schema). The 15 `_Lock*` assertions then become unnecessary and delete. Exported names and their structural shapes are unchanged, so no consumer edits.

removes_failure_path.justification: The `_Lock*` Assert<Equals<>> lines are a compile-time validation guard; deleting them removes a check. It is safe only because the guard becomes tautological once the type is derived from the schema — but the honest answer is that a guard is removed.

steps: Replace one interface at a time with a z.infer alias; the existing `_Lock*` assertion for it stays in place during the swap and must still compile — if it errors, the interface and schema were already subtly different and that difference is a real finding.

Once all are aliases, delete schemas.ts:440-472 and run `pnpm typecheck` at the repo root — apps/server/src/ws-protocol.ts and apps/web/src/lib/ws/protocol-types.ts both re-export these names and will catch any shape change.
`pnpm --filter @ledrums/protocol run test` — schemas.test.ts pins the runtime parse behaviour, which must be untouched.
